proof.criterion: Review round two, the push_failed minor: a push that may have landed is retried once and no more, while the two causes that push nothing keep the window's whole allowance.
proof.surface: The listener's delivery handler over a real durable at the production window (defaultUnplaceableRetryWindow), with the pushes counted at the transport.
proof.observed: Green in the package run. At the default 60 s window - twelve deferrals for the other causes - the push-failed message is deferred once at attempt 1 with reason push_failed and window_deferrals 1, given up at attempt 2 under unplaceable_push_failed, and the transport counted exactly 2 pushes. So a push that landed but was not answered is repeated at most once. The no-record message on the same harness and in the same window is deferred again at attempt 2 with window_deferrals 12 and not given up, which is the test's own control: the give-up at attempt 2 is the push bound, not a window that ran out. The declined alternative - a dedupe entry instead of a deferral bound - would have made the redelivery an attempt-dedupe skip and stopped push_failed being retried at all, which delivery.go's own attempt-cache branch shows.
proof.negativeControl: Removing the cap (`windowDeferrals = min(windowDeferrals, pushFailedDeferrals)` made unreachable) fails the test: 'timed out waiting for the push-failed message to be given up' after 20.52s - at the default window it would have gone on deferring. Reverted.
